cases.description: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a localized dilation of the abdominal aorta, typically defined as a diameter greater than 3 cm, which can lead to rupture and significant morbidity or mortality.
cases.name: abdominal aortic aneurysm

cases.description: An anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear is a partial or complete disruption of the ACL of the knee, typically resulting from a pivoting or hyperextension injury, and is a common cause of knee instability.
cases.name: anterior cruciate ligament tear

cases.description: Acute appendicitis is inflammation of the vermiform appendix, typically presenting with right lower quadrant pain, and diagnosed on imaging by an enlarged, thick-walled, hyperenhancing appendix with surrounding inflammatory changes.
cases.name: acute appendicitis

cases.description: Aortic dissection is a critical condition characterized by the separation of the aortic wall layers due to an intimal tear, resulting in an intramural hematoma and potential rupture; it often presents with severe, acute chest or back pain and may lead to life-threatening complications.
cases.name: aortic dissection

cases.description: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is the non-neoplastic enlargement of the prostate gland due to stromal and glandular hyperplasia, commonly seen in older men, resulting in lower urinary tract symptoms and visible as an enlarged prostate on imaging.
cases.name: benign prostatic hyperplasia

cases.description: The Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) assessment is a standardized classification system for mammographic, ultrasound, and MRI breast findings, assigning a category from 0 to 6 to guide clinical management.

index_codes.display: Breast Imaging and Reporting and Data System

cases.name: BI-RADS assessment

cases.description: Breast density refers to the proportion of fatty tissue to fibroglandular tissue in the breast as seen on a mammogram.
cases.name: Breast density

cases.description: Cardiomegaly is the enlargement of the cardiac silhouette on imaging, typically defined as a cardiothoracic ratio greater than 0.5 on a PA chest radiograph, and may reflect chamber enlargement, pericardial effusion, or myocardial disease.
cases.name: cardiomegaly

cases.description: Cerebral infarction is the irreversible death of brain tissue due to ischemia, typically from arterial occlusion, visible on imaging as a region of restricted diffusion acutely and encephalomalacia chronically.
cases.name: cerebral infarction

cases.description: Cervical lymphadenopathy is the enlargement of lymph nodes in the neck region, which may be reactive, infectious, or neoplastic in origin, and is evaluated by size, morphology, and enhancement pattern on imaging.
cases.name: cervical lymphadenopathy

cases.description: Coronary artery calcification is the deposition of calcium within the walls of the coronary arteries, a marker of atherosclerotic disease, commonly quantified by Agatston score on non-contrast CT.
cases.name: coronary artery calcification

cases.description: A distal radius fracture is a break in the distal end of the radius bone near the wrist joint, one of the most common fractures in clinical practice, typically resulting from a fall on an outstretched hand.

index_codes.display: Fracture of distal end of radius

cases.name: distal radius fracture

cases.description: An FDG-avid pulmonary nodule is a lung nodule demonstrating elevated fluorodeoxyglucose uptake on PET imaging, raising concern for malignancy and requiring further characterization or tissue sampling.
cases.name: FDG-avid pulmonary nodule

cases.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary malignant tumor of the liver, typically arising in the setting of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis, characterized on imaging by arterial hyperenhancement with washout in the portal venous or delayed phases.
cases.name: hepatocellular carcinoma

cases.description: Hip osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, and joint space narrowing of the hip joint.
cases.name: hip osteoarthritis

cases.description: Intracranial hemorrhage is the presence of blood within the cranial vault, which may occur in the epidural, subdural, subarachnoid, intraparenchymal, or intraventricular compartments.
cases.name: intracranial hemorrhage

cases.description: A kidney stone (renal calculus) is a solid concretion formed from crystallized minerals and salts within the renal collecting system, visible on CT as a hyperdense focus within the kidney or ureter.
cases.name: kidney stone

cases.description: Hepatic hemangioma is the most common benign tumor of the liver, composed of vascular channels lined by endothelium, characteristically demonstrating peripheral nodular enhancement with progressive centripetal fill-in on contrast-enhanced imaging.
cases.name: hepatic hemangioma

cases.description: Lumbar disc herniation is the displacement of disc material beyond the intervertebral disc space in the lumbar spine, which may result in compression of adjacent neural structures and associated radiculopathy.

index_codes.display: Herniation of nucleus pulposus of lumbar intervertebral disc

cases.name: lumbar disc herniation

cases.description: A meningioma is a typically benign, slow-growing tumor arising from the meningeal coverings of the brain or spinal cord, commonly appearing as an extra-axial, homogeneously enhancing, dural-based mass on imaging.
cases.name: meningioma

cases.description: Motion artifact is image degradation caused by patient movement during acquisition, resulting in blurring, ghosting, or misregistration that may limit diagnostic interpretation.
cases.name: motion artifact

cases.description: An ovarian cyst is a fluid-filled sac within or on the surface of an ovary, which may be physiologic (follicular or corpus luteum) or pathologic, commonly detected incidentally on pelvic imaging in women of reproductive age.
cases.name: ovarian cyst

cases.description: Pericardial effusion is the accumulation of fluid within the pericardial sac surrounding the heart, which may be serous, hemorrhagic, or exudative, and can range from a small physiologic amount to a large hemodynamically significant collection.
cases.name: pericardial effusion

cases.description: Pleural effusion is the accumulation of fluid in the pleural space, visible on imaging as dependent opacity with a meniscus sign on upright radiography or as layering fluid on cross-sectional imaging.
cases.name: pleural effusion

cases.description: Pneumothorax is the presence of air in the pleural space, which may be spontaneous, traumatic, or iatrogenic, and is identified on imaging as a visceral pleural line with absent lung markings peripherally.
cases.name: pneumothorax

cases.description: Primary lung malignancy is a malignant neoplasm arising from the lung parenchyma or bronchial tree, most commonly non-small cell carcinoma, presenting as a mass, nodule, or infiltrate on imaging.
cases.name: primary lung malignancy

cases.description: Pulmonary embolism is the occlusion of a pulmonary artery or one of its branches, typically caused by thrombi that originate from the deep veins of the legs or other parts of the body, leading to impaired gas exchange and potential hemodynamic instability.
cases.name: pulmonary embolism

cases.description: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis is a condition of infancy characterized by hypertrophy of the pyloric muscle, resulting in gastric outlet obstruction and projectile nonbilious vomiting, diagnosed by ultrasound demonstrating increased pyloric muscle thickness and channel length.
cases.name: hypertrophic pyloric stenosis

cases.description: A rib fracture is a break in the continuity of one or more ribs, typically resulting from trauma, visible on imaging as a cortical disruption or lucent line through the rib.

cases.description: A rotator cuff tear is a partial or complete disruption of one or more tendons of the rotator cuff muscles, most commonly the supraspinatus, resulting in shoulder pain and weakness, diagnosed by MRI or ultrasound.

cases.description: Spinal stenosis is the narrowing of the spinal canal, lateral recesses, or neural foramina, typically from degenerative changes including disc bulging, facet hypertrophy, and ligamentum flavum thickening, resulting in compression of neural structures.

cases.description: A subdural hematoma is a collection of blood in the subdural space between the dura mater and arachnoid membrane, typically resulting from tearing of bridging veins due to trauma or in the setting of coagulopathy.
cases.name: subdural hematoma

cases.description: A thyroid nodule is a discrete lesion within the thyroid gland that is radiologically distinct from the surrounding thyroid parenchyma, commonly detected incidentally on imaging and evaluated by ultrasound for malignancy risk.
cases.name: thyroid nodule

cases.description: Uterine leiomyoma (fibroid) is a benign smooth muscle tumor of the uterus, the most common pelvic tumor in women, appearing as a well-circumscribed mass with variable signal intensity on MRI depending on cellularity and degeneration.
